subject: Clarify remediation ETA and evidence: session token & auth findings
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-07T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: pen test report + remediation ETA for auth/session findings

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for hosting the pen test report yesterday. Our security team has a few follow-ups on the auth-related findings (notably session token replay possibility, long-lived tokens, and gaps in authz logging). Can you please: 

- Confirm you can share the final pen test report summary (redacted is fine) and current remediation status for the items above.
- Provide an ETA for proof-of-fix / evidence (config snippets, logs, patch diffs) for the session/token and authz gaps.
- Confirm whether remediation will include additional logging / alert rules we can validate.

We need this evidence to close the SIG questionnaire for our audit next month. If you can point to a single deliverable or a short timeline this week that would be great.

Thanks,
Oliver Chen
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security@acme.com

Attachment: acme-pt-findings.xlsx (referenced list of findings)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-07T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + remediation ETA for auth/session findings

Hi Oliver — thanks for the note and the findings sheet. We can absolutely provide a summarized pen test report and targeted evidence for the auth/session findings. High-level plan: 

- I will attach the redwood_pt_report_summary.pdf (redacted) and a remediation timeline.
- Session token replay: engineering has a patch candidate and will provide a patch diff + unit/integration test logs. ETA for evidence handoff: 2027-04-12.
- Long-lived tokens / rotation: rotation policy change is scheduled, ETA for proof (policy + config Screenshot) 2027-04-15.
- Authz logging: adding request-level audit events and a Kibana sample export; ETA 2027-04-14.

If you need anything sooner (e.g., an interim validation artifact), let me know and I can ask the team to prioritize a focused export. We can also schedule a 30-min review once the artifacts are ready.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_pt_report_summary.pdf (redacted)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: pen test report + remediation ETA for auth/session findings

Jonas / team — status update and specifics below. Attaching the core artifacts for the session token fix and the remediation timeline.

Summary per finding: 
- Session token replay (owner: marcus_lin) — root cause: inconsistent token invalidation on concurrent logout path. Fix: coordinated server-side session invalidation + tightened token TTL for refresh tokens. Evidence to provide: session-fix-patch.diff (included), unit/integration test logs (sanitized), and an exec log showing token invalidation on logout. ETA for handoff: 2027-04-12 10:00 PDT.

- Long-lived tokens / rotation (owner: laura_bennett) — Laura to provide updated token rotation policy doc + a config screenshot of the new TTL/rotation mapping. ETA: 2027-04-15 EOD.

- Authz logging (owner: irene_choi) — Adding request-level audit events for privilege changes and failed permission checks; will export a sample Kibana .ndjson and a short query snippet for their SIEM. ETA: 2027-04-14 16:00 PDT.

Evidence delivery plan: single bundled handoff of artifacts to Acme security via secure upload: 2027-04-12 (session artifacts) and remaining items by 2027-04-15. For each artifact we will include a short README that describes what to look for.

Attachments (included): 
- session-fix-patch.diff (patch diff, 8 KB)
- remediation_timeline_v2.xlsx (timeline with owners & dates)
- redwood_pt_report_summary.pdf (already shared)

If Acme needs signed statements or additional screenshots from production can be arranged under NDA.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
